S.FORM: sua tia=kari=maku ia, tee=ku pu-isua Suŋau mata ʔusu ŋanai-ini.
S.PHON: sua tiakarimaku ia teeku puisua suŋau mata ʔusu ŋanaiini
S.FORM: sua tiakarimaku ia, teeku puisua Sungau mata 'usu nganaiini.
S.PHON: sua tiaka[r|ɾ]imaku ia teeku puisua suŋau mata ʔusu ŋanaiini
S.TRANSL: I am going to tell the story of the Sungau and (a woman) called 'Usu.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: sua tia=kari=maku ia, tia=ku pu-isua Suŋau mata ʔusu ŋanai-ini.
S.PHON: sua tiakarimaku ia tiaku puisua suŋau mata ʔusu ŋanaiini
S.FORM: sua tiakarimaku ia, tiaku puisua Sungau mata 'usu nganaiini.
S.PHON: sua tiaka[r|ɾ]imaku ia tiaku puisua suŋau mata ʔusu ŋanaiini
S.TRANSL: I am going to tell the story of the Sungau and (a woman) called 'Usu.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: ni-pusu-ʔuma=kan piniŋ ʔusu mu-usa ʔuma-ʔuma, pureren=kan sua ʔusu.
S.PHON: nipusuʔumakan piniŋ ʔusu muusa ʔumaʔuma purerenkan sua ʔusu
nipusuʔumakan piniŋ ʔusu muusa ʔumaʔuma pu[r|ɾ]e[r|ɾ]enkan sua ʔusu
S.TRANSL: When her neighbors had come to the fields to help with the crop, 'Usu watched them stealthily.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: ni-pusu-ʔuma=kan piniŋ ʔusu mu-a-kusa ʔuma-ʔuma, pureren=kan sua ʔusu.
S.PHON: nipusuʔumakan piniŋ ʔusu muakusa ʔumaʔuma purerenkan sua ʔusu
nipusuʔumakan piniŋ ʔusu muakusa ʔumaʔuma pu[r|ɾ]e[r|ɾ]enkan sua ʔusu
S.TRANSL: When her neighbors had come to the fields to help with the crop, 'Usu watched them stealthily.

S.FORM: "ʔa, tee=ku mu-a-taruʔan, cina," misa=kani sua ʔusu.
S.PHON: ʔa teeku muataruʔan tʂina misakani sua ʔusu
ʔa teeku muata[r|ɾ]uʔan tʂina misakani sua ʔusu
S.TRANSL: "Ah! I want to pass the night (in the field), Mother," said 'Usu.
Her mother replied, "The Sungau will come there."
"Ah! (But) I'll make a campfire"
Evening had come.
(It turned out that) 'Usu would indeed pass the night (in the field).
(When) it was already near dusk, 'Usu make a campfire.

S.FORM: maka-sua=cu ma-pitəʔə=cu, cili-cili-ai=kan sua ʔusu canum-ini.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu mapitəʔəʦu tʂiɾitʂiɾiaikan sua ʔusu ʦanumini
makasuaʦu mapiteʔeʦu tʂi[r|ɾ]itʂi[r|ɾ]iaikan sua ʔusu ʦanumini
S.TRANSL: (When) it was already dark, 'Usu had her water spilled.
(When) it was already nearly dark, the Sungau came out.
"'Usu, have you got water?"

S.FORM: "ʔa. ʔakia canum=aku. ʔacu c<in>ili-cili cau mi-caʔania," misa=kan.
S.PHON: ʔa ʔakia ʦanumaku ʔaʦu tʂiniɾitʂiɾi ʦau miʦaʔania misakan
ʔa ʔakia ʦanumaku ʔaʦu tʂini[r|ɾ]itʂi[r|ɾ]i ʦau miʦaʔania misakan
S.TRANSL: "I've got no (more) water (lit, my water is no more), somebody had spilled it this afternoon," said (she).
(And) she pinched her child with her fingernails.
"Please fetch (some) water," said the Sungau.

S.FORM: pasə-kə-kəəc-ai=kan sua ʔusu manu-ini, si kaʔan=kan tia=pa-tiʔin=kiai.
S.PHON: pasəkəkəəʦaikan sua ʔusu manuini ʂi kaʔankan tiapatiʔinkiai
S.FORM: pasekekeecaikan sua 'usu manuini, si ka'ankan tiapati'inkiai.
S.PHON: pasekekeeʦaikan sua ʔusu manuini ʂi kaʔankan tiapatiʔinkiai
S.TRANSL: She pinched her child with her fingernails, for she wasn't going to leave it behind.

S.PHON: vuau ʔikua naamumaku muʦanumapakan misakan suŋau
vuau ʔikua naamumaku muʦanumapakan misakan suŋau
S.TRANSL: "Give me my grandchild and (go to) fetch water," said the Sungau.

S.FORM: pasə-kəəc-ən=kan ʔusu manu-ini, si kaʔan tia=pa-tiʔin=kiai.
S.PHON: pasəkəəʦənkan ʔusu manuini ʂi kaʔan tiapatiʔinkiai
pasekeeʦenkan ʔusu manuini ʂi kaʔan tiapatiʔinkiai
S.TRANSL: 'Usu pinched her child with her fingernails, for she wasn't going to leave it behind.
'Usu left, grabbing (with the bamboo) water-bucket as he passed.
She picked out a body louse and put it on a stone.

S.FORM: "nuu ʔusu misa=kan kasua Suŋau ia, 'əəʔə,' kisa-u-i=ʔai."
S.PHON: nuu ʔusu misakan kasua suŋau ia əəʔə kisauiʔai
nuu ʔusu misakan kasua suŋau ia ʔeeʔeʔ kisauiʔai
S.TRANSL: "When the Sungau says 'Usu to you, say 'Yes,' in reply."
Thereupon, 'Usu left for home.

S.FORM: "ʔacu nanu si ʔusu tia=mu-a-canumu," misa=kan sua Suŋau.
S.PHON: ʔaʦu nanu ʂi ʔusu tiamuaʦanumu misakan sua suŋau
S.FORM: "'acu nanu si 'usu tiamuacanumu," misakan sua Sungau.
S.PHON: ʔaʦu nanu ʂi ʔusu tiamuaʦanumu misakan sua suŋau
S.TRANSL: "Where is 'Usu, for she would (go to) fetch water?" said the Sungau.
Walking down the road, he called out in passing, "'Usu!"

S.FORM: "ʔusu, ʔusu" misa, "əəʔə" misa=kan iisua na canumu.
S.PHON: ʔusu ʔusu misa əəʔə misakan iisua na ʦanumu
ʔusu ʔusu misa eeʔe misakan iisua na ʦanumu
S.TRANSL: As he called "'Usu!" "'Usu!", that one from the water said, "Yes."
Thereupon, he came to the place of drawing water.

S.PHON: ʔusu misa əəʔə misakan sua ʔusu
ʔusu misa eeʔe misakan sua ʔusu
S.TRANSL: As he called, "'Usu!", 'Usu said "Yes."

S.FORM: ma-kasi=kan ʔinia, "ʔusu" misa, "əəʔə" misa=kan ʔeesi na vaatu.
S.PHON: makaʂikan ʔinia ʔusu misa əəʔə misakan ʔeeʂi na vaatu
makaʂikan ʔinia ʔusu misa eeʔe misakan ʔeeʂi na vaatu
S.TRANSL: Going there, he called, "'Usu!", (and) the one from the stone (lit., the being- from-the-stone) said "Yes."

S.FORM: ʔuriŋ-ai=kan ʔinia sua vaatu, ʔaisi=kan ʔinia caracə.
S.PHON: ʔuriŋaikan ʔinia sua vaatu ʔaiʂikan ʔinia ʦaraʦə
ʔu[r|ɾ]iŋaikan ʔinia sua vaatu ʔaiʂikan ʔinia ʦa[r|ɾ]aʦe
S.TRANSL: As he lit a torch (and directed it) upon the stone, there was the louse.
(And) the Sungau squeezed the body louse dead between his fingernails.
"'Usu!" he called. No (reply).
Thereupon, the Sungau followed her home.

S.FORM: ŋuai=kan=cu ni-aluma vai ʔusu sua Suŋau.
S.PHON: ŋuaikanʦu niaɾuma vai ʔusu sua suŋau
ŋuaikanʦu nia[r|ɾ]uma vai ʔusu sua suŋau
S.TRANSL: Lying already in wait for the Sungau had been 'Usu's older brother.
Her older brother ambushed and hit the Sungau (in the head).

S.FORM: ka-ʔala-ʔalam-ai=kan sua vai-ini, aranai=kani ʔinia sua kan ma-a-ŋaliŋali maamia sua ʔalam-ini sikəlapə talakuluka tanaveciŋal avalaʔi maamia kula-kula-kulai ni-aranai=kan ʔinia ka-vaŋvaŋ.
S.PHON: kaʔaɾaʔaɾamaikan sua vaiini aranaikani ʔinia sua kan maaŋaɾiŋaɾi maamia sua ʔaɾamini ʂikəɾapə taɾakuɾuka tanavetʂiŋaɾ avaɾaʔi maamia kuɾakuɾakuɾai niaranaikan ʔinia kavaŋvaŋ
S.FORM: ka'ara'aramaikan sua vaiini, aranaikani 'inia sua kan maangaringari maamia sua 'aramini sikerape tarakuruka tanavecingar avara'i maamia kurakurakurai niaranaikan 'inia kavangvang.
S.PHON: kaʔa[r|ɾ]aʔa[r|ɾ]amaikan sua vaiini a[r|ɾ]anaikani ʔinia sua kan maaŋa[r|ɾ]iŋa[r|ɾ]i maamia sua ʔa[r|ɾ]amini ʂike[r|ɾ]ape ta[r|ɾ]aku[r|ɾ]uka tanavetʂiŋa[r|ɾ] ava[r|ɾ]aʔi maamia ku[r|ɾ]aku[r|ɾ]aku[r|ɾ]ai nia[r|ɾ]anaikan ʔinia kavaŋvaŋ
S.TRANSL: As her older brother cut (it) open, there came out from its shaking flesh mosquitos, insects, and all kinds of worms.
The worms came out of the defecation.
That's all I know (about the story).
